question: What does the writ 'Habeas- Corpus' in the Indian Judicial system literally mean?
solution:
The correct answer is __**You shall have the body**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The writ of **Habeas Corpus** literally means **"You shall have the body"**.
 
• It is a fundamental right in the Indian Judicial system to protect individuals from unlawful detention.
 
• This writ is issued to produce the detained person before the court to examine the legality of the detention.
 
• The objective is to ensure that no person is detained without lawful justification.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The writ of **Habeas Corpus** is a vital safeguard against arbitrary detention and is enshrined in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, which guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty.
 
• It can be filed by the detained person or any person on their behalf.
 
• The importance of this writ is underscored by its role in upholding the rule of law and ensuring that individual freedoms are not infringed upon without due process.
 
• Various landmark cases in India have highlighted the significance of the writ of Habeas Corpus in protecting human rights.
